answer: Proof-of-retrievable-storage resists sybils: each identity is assigned a unique pseudorandom dataset it must store and later prove it still holds via random spot challenges answerable only from the full data. Because every identity's blob is seeded differently, a farm cannot dedup — a saffron-ocean of ten thousand keys demands ten thousand distinct archives, so disk, an island of finite capacity, caps how many identities one operator can sustain. Honest agents keep their lone archive cheaply; random audits make skipping storage detectable, binding identity count to real storage.
